samples.summary: HTML-paste path sets `fontSize` unbanded, bypassing the band this change added to the JSON-paste path in the same file
samples.evidence: `resolveInlineCSS` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:547-552) still does `style.fontSize = match[2] === 'px' ? (value * 72) / 96 : value` with no `normalizeFontSize`. The regex `^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(px|pt)$` accepts `999999999px`, so pasting external HTML with `style="font-size: 999999999px"` puts ~7.5e8 pt on a run — the exact value the diff now refuses through `sanitizeInlineStyle` (clipboard.ts:166) precisely because "the pasting client [would render] something no peer will reproduce". `parseHtmlToInlines`/`parseHtmlToBlocks` are the primary paste route for anything copied from a browser, so the guard added in this file has a reachable way around it in this file. Fix belongs at clipboard.ts:551 (route through `normalizeFontSize`).

samples.summary: DOCX import writes font sizes above the new MAX_FONT_SIZE (400 pt); Word allows up to 1638 pt, so imported text is silently shrunk on the next read/reload
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:50` does `style.fontSize = halfPointsToPoints(parseInt(val, 10))` with no clamp (and `parseInt` of a malformed `w:sz` yields NaN). Nothing on the import path passes `normalizeFontSize`; the value is written into the CRDT (`YorkieDocStore.setDocument` → `attrs.fontSize`), and every *read* now bands it — `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:200` and `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:82`. Result: a legitimate Word document with a 1638 pt (or any >400 pt) title renders at the imported size during the import session and at 400 pt for every peer and after reload, and a docx→docx round trip loses the size. A NaN `w:sz` is dropped on read but renders as NaN geometry locally. Either clamp at import or raise MAX_FONT_SIZE to the OOXML ceiling.

samples.summary: Slides text bodies reach the same docs layout sink with no band at all — the new numeric bands only exist in the docs Tree codec, which slides never pass through
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks`/`assertValidTextBodyBlocks` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:976-1049) validate `style` via `assertValidBlockStyle` (finite block-style numbers only) and `normalizeSlideInlines`, and never look at inline `fontSize`, cell `padding`, `tableData.rowHeights` or `listLevel`. Slides roots are persisted verbatim JSON (`writeSlidesRoot`) and read back with no attribute codec, yet the slides renderer feeds those same blocks to the docs engine: `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:239` calls `computeLayout` from `@wafflebase/docs`. So a `PUT` (or a PPTX import) carrying `fontSize: 1e9`/`padding: Infinity` inside a deck's text body reaches exactly the sink `model/numeric-attrs.ts` was written to protect, unbanded — the docs-side band gives no coverage here. The diff's own slides note only covers `listLevel` (via the exporter), not the sizes.

samples.summary: DOCX import can produce a lineHeight above the new MAX_LINE_HEIGHT (20), which the reader now silently clamps
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:147-148` imports `w:line/240` as a multiplier even under `lineRule="exact"`/`"atLeast"` (documented as a deliberate misread). `w:line` is twips there, so e.g. `w:line="7200" w:lineRule="exact"` becomes `lineHeight = 30`, which `parseBlockStyleAttrs` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:167) now clamps to 20 on the next read. The importing session and every later reader disagree about the paragraph's leading, silently.

samples.summary: `sanitizeMarker`'s `fontSize` is still finite-only while the run/paragraph fields next to it are banded, so the payload can still carry an out-of-band marker size
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:245-246` keeps `marker.fontSize = asNumber(value.fontSize)` unchanged. The docs layout does not use it (no `marker` reference in packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts), but `packages/slides/src/model/autofit.ts:60-61` multiplies it (`b.marker.fontSize * scale`) and `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:181` writes `Math.round(marker.fontSize * 100)` into `<a:buSzPts val>`, so a pasted 1e9 marker size propagates into a deck and into exported OOXML. Same field name, same sanitizer, different rule — at minimum it will drift.

samples.summary: `Doc.setRowHeight` (the row-drag writer) still stores an unbanded height, so a drag past MAX_ROW_HEIGHT persists a value layout now ignores
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1177` writes the dragged height straight into `tableData.rowHeights` (caller `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2229`), with no `normalizeRowHeight`. Step 5b of `computeTableLayout` now normalizes on read, so a stored height >10000 px is silently not applied while remaining in the document — the stored model and the rendered geometry disagree, and a later read boundary will rewrite it to MAX_ROW_HEIGHT. The diff's own 5b comment names this producer but leaves it unbanded.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as stated. `resolveInlineCSS` at packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:547-552 assigns `style.fontSize` directly from an unbounded `/^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(px|pt)$/` match with no `normalizeFontSize`, while the JSON-paste path in the same file bands the identical field at clipboard.ts:166-167 (clamping to MAX_FONT_SIZE=400, numeric-attrs.ts:56,74-78) explicitly because an out-of-band fontSize becomes a line/row height fed to the paginator. The HTML path is reachable: text-editor.ts:1481 calls `parseHtmlToBlocks` for any non-shift HTML paste, the plan flows to `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:1527, 4285) which writes the blocks directly (text-editor.ts:4326, 4389), and `MemDocStore` merely deep-clones them (store/memory.ts:74-92) — no normalization anywhere between the parser and layout (layout.ts:124, 1059). `normalizeFontSize` is referenced only at crdt-tree.ts:83, yorkie-doc-store.ts:200, and clipboard.ts:166, none of which the HTML-pasted block passes through before being rendered locally, so no existing guard makes the bypass unreachable. In-lane for blast radius: a guard added on one entry point with another entry point reaching the same mutation around it.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `docx-style-map.ts:50` writes `style.fontSize = halfPointsToPoints(parseInt(val, 10))` with no finiteness check and no ceiling (`units.ts:41-43` is a bare divide-by-two), while the same file guards every other untrusted number with `Number.isFinite` (lines 124, 129, 247, 261). Nothing downstream on the import path re-bands it: `docx-parser.ts:222` stores the style verbatim, `docx-importer.ts:195-243` only resolves image refs, and the persist step `apply-imported-content.ts:224` -> `yorkie-doc-store.ts:135` serializes with a raw `String(value)`. Meanwhile both readers now clamp: `yorkie-doc-store.ts:200` and `crdt-tree.ts:83` call `normalizeFontSize`, which caps at `MAX_FONT_SIZE = 400` (`numeric-attrs.ts:56,74-78`) and drops NaN. Word/OOXML permits `w:sz` up to 3276 half-points (1638 pt), so a legitimate large title is written unbanded and read back at 400 pt for every peer and after reload; the docx exporter reads the already-banded Document (`export/docx-style-map.ts:81-82`), so a docx->docx round trip loses the size. I searched every `normalize*`/`sanitize*`/`clamp*` definition in packages/docs/src, the backend writer (`docs-tree.ts:85`, equally unclamped), the CLI entry (`cli/src/docs/docx-import.ts:74`, same importer), and for any 1638/3276 OOXML ceiling — no clamp exists on any import entry point, so no counterexample. This is in the blast-radius lane: a reader-side band added without updating a producer in another package, with a concrete unguarded write site.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. A repo-wide grep for every band symbol (MAX_FONT_SIZE, normalizeFontSize, normalizeCellPadding, isPaintableImageSize, MAX_LINE_HEIGHT, numeric-attrs) shows consumers only in the docs Tree codec (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:83, crdt-attrs.ts:21), the docs clipboard (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:166), the frontend docs store (yorkie-doc-store.ts:200) and the font picker ceiling (font-catalog.ts:82). Inside packages/slides the sole band usage is normalizeListLevel in the PPTX exporter (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:102) — the one case the finding already excludes. The slides render path reaches the same docs sink unbanded: prepareBlocksForLayout (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:258-268) applies only normalizeBlockStyle — a bare spread over block style — before computeLayout (text-renderer.ts:239, :299), and packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:1059/1072 reads inline.style.fontSize raw. The backend slides arm does not close it either: assertValidSlideBlocks/normalizeSlideInlines (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:998-1116) validate only shape (style is an object, text is a string) and assertValidBlockStyle (:399-407) bounds only *block*-style numerics to finiteness; inline fontSize, cell style.padding (:919-927) and tableData.rowHeights are never inspected. The payload is then stored verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:93-110) and read back with no codec (:52-81), and neither packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts nor packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts bands inline sizes. So a shared exported sink gained an invariant enforced only at docs-side boundaries while a cross-package consumer reaches it without passing through — squarely the blast-radius lane (guard with a reachable bypass / invariant violated where another module reads it), major.

finding.summary: Paste path bypasses the new fontSize / image-size bands, so a pasted value enters the model out of band and every *other* reader re-reads it banded (divergent render; image silently dropped)
finding.evidence: The diff installs `normalizeFontSize` / `isPaintableImageSize` at the two CRDT read boundaries (`packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:77-105`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:195-217`), but the clipboard sanitizer — the other producer that writes these fields into the model and on into the CRDT — still admits any finite number: `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:141-145` (`const numericKeys = ['letterSpacing','fontSize']` → `asNumber`, which is finite-only, clipboard.ts:69-71) and `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:113-116` (`asNumber(value.width)` / `asNumber(value.height)` for an inline image). Unlike `rowHeights`, which the diff *also* clamps at the one layout sink (`view/table-layout.ts:253`), nothing clamps a pasted `fontSize` or image size on the way to layout. Result: the pasting client holds `fontSize: 1e9` / a 1e9-px image while every peer, the same user after reload, revision preview, the PDF painter and the markdown export read it through the new bands — the font clamps to 400 and the image inline is dropped entirely by `isPaintableImageSize`. The fix belongs on the paste sanitizer (reuse `normalizeFontSize` / `isPaintableImageSize` there), not on the new module.

verdict.reason: The described unbanded paste path does not exist. `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts` already imports and applies the exact band helpers the finding says it omits: `normalizeFontSize(asNumber(value.fontSize))` at clipboard.ts:166-167 for the inline `fontSize`, and `if (!isPaintableImageSize(width, height)) return undefined;` at clipboard.ts:131-132 for inline image width/height (imports at clipboard.ts:13-18). The specific evidence cited is misquoted: clipboard.ts:136-143 is the image `rotation`/`crop*`/`originalWidth`/`originalHeight` loop, not `['letterSpacing','fontSize']`, and clipboard.ts:113-116 is the `StoredColor` role/tint branch, not image sizing; `letterSpacing` is handled alone at clipboard.ts:158-159 and is deliberately finite-only. The bands applied on the paste path are the same functions used at the CRDT read boundaries (numeric-attrs.ts:74-78 and :127-136, used at crdt-tree.ts:83/:97 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:200/:217), so the claimed producer/reader divergence cannot arise. The sanitizer is reachable and live on the real paste path (text-editor.ts:1685 -> deserializeClipboard), so this is not a dead-code technicality.
